policy.admission: Source-identified portraits and authored works; explicit image reuse evidence; no generated historical likenesses.

title.zh: 侧面肖像中的牛顿纪念

alt.en: An etched profile of Newton sits inside a circular frame above an identifying inscription.
alt.zh: 牛顿的蚀刻侧面肖像置于圆框之中，下方有身份题记。

caption.en: W. Hoare’s etching is dated 1734, seven years after Newton’s death. Its medallion-like format presents the mathematician as a figure for public remembrance.
caption.zh: W.霍尔的蚀刻画作于1734年，即牛顿逝世七年后。奖章般的构图将这位数学家塑造成供公众纪念的人物。

interpretation.en: The classical profile and Latin lettering give scientific authorship a commemorative form. Compare this later image with Newton’s mathematical writing and institutional career.
interpretation.zh: 古典侧面构图与拉丁题字，为科学作者赋予纪念形式。可将这幅后世图像与牛顿的数学著作及机构生涯对读。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Wellcome Collection.
note.zh: 公有领域图像。署名：惠康收藏馆（Wellcome Collection）。

alt.en: A coloured oval portrait shows Copernicus in a fur-trimmed garment above a small medallion and printed name.
alt.zh: 彩色椭圆肖像中，哥白尼穿着饰有毛皮的衣服，下方有小奖章与印刷姓名。

caption.en: John Chapman’s coloured stipple engraving dates to 1802, more than two centuries after Copernicus’s death.
caption.zh: 约翰·查普曼的彩色点刻版画作于1802年，比哥白尼逝世晚两个多世纪。

interpretation.en: The print shows how a recognisable author’s face accompanied the later circulation of scientific reputation. It belongs to Copernicus’s reception rather than the making of his planetary model.
interpretation.zh: 这幅版画展示了鲜明的作者面孔如何伴随科学声誉传播。它属于哥白尼的后世接受史，而非其行星模型形成时的图像。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Wellcome Collection.

alt.en: A coloured lithograph portrays Nightingale in a pale bonnet and striped shawl tied with a blue bow.
alt.zh: 彩色石版画中的南丁格尔戴浅色帽子，披条纹披肩，系蓝色蝴蝶结。

caption.en: H. M. Bonham-Carter made this coloured lithograph in 1854, the year Nightingale travelled to the Crimean War hospitals.
caption.zh: H. M.博纳姆-卡特于1854年制作这幅彩色石版画；同年南丁格尔前往克里米亚战争医院。

interpretation.en: A composed personal portrait offers a different starting point from the familiar lamp-bearing emblem. Her public work also depended on records, training and hospital organization.
interpretation.zh: 这幅沉静的人物肖像，为理解南丁格尔提供了不同于“提灯者”象征的起点。她的公共工作也依赖记录、培训与医院组织。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Wellcome Collection.
note.zh: 公有领域图像。署名：惠康收藏馆（Wellcome Collection）。

alt.en: A veiled woman holds an open book inside a rectangular engraved frame with a name panel below.
alt.zh: 戴面纱的女子手持打开的书，置于长方形雕版画框内，下方有姓名栏。

caption.en: William Marshall’s engraving dates to 1642, centuries after Hildegard of Bingen. The book and religious clothing construct the image of a learned abbess.
caption.zh: 威廉·马歇尔的雕版画作于1642年，比宾根的希尔德加德生活的时代晚数百年。书本与宗教服饰共同塑造博学女修院长的形象。

interpretation.en: Read the book and identifying text as choices made by a later printmaker. Hildegard’s surviving letters provide a separate route into her own community and voice.
interpretation.zh: 书本与身份题字体现后世版画家的选择；希尔德加德存世的书信，则提供通往她本人社群与声音的另一条路径。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Wellcome Collection.
note.zh: 公有领域图像。署名：惠康收藏馆（Wellcome Collection）。

alt.en: Watt sits beside a table, resting his head on one hand in a black-and-white engraved portrait.
alt.zh: 黑白雕版肖像中，瓦特坐在桌旁，一只手托着头。

caption.en: This 1792 engraving follows a portrait by Carl Frederik von Breda. The engraver is not identified in the collection record.
caption.zh: 这幅1792年雕版画依据卡尔·弗雷德里克·冯·布雷达的肖像而作；馆藏记录未注明雕刻者。

interpretation.en: The image gives a face to the engineer named in the separate-condenser story. The contemplative pose is a portrait convention, not a record of the 1769 invention.
interpretation.zh: 图像为独立冷凝器故事中的工程师提供面孔。沉思姿态是一种肖像惯例，并非1769年发明现场的记录。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Wellcome Collection.
note.zh: 公有领域图像。署名：惠康收藏馆（Wellcome Collection）。

title.en: A medical scene on a copy of Ibn Sina’s Canon
title.zh: 伊本·西那《医典》抄本封板上的医疗场景

alt.en: A brightly painted manuscript binding shows a reclining woman, a seated physician and attendants beneath a tree.
alt.zh: 鲜艳的抄本装帧画中，一名女子斜卧，医者坐在旁边，侍从立于树下。

caption.en: Wellcome identifies this as the binding board of a manuscript of Avicenna’s Canon of Medicine, showing a doctor taking a woman’s pulse. Its catalogue does not date the binding or name the painter.
caption.zh: 惠康将其识别为阿维森纳《医典》抄本的封板，描绘医者为女子诊脉。目录未注明封板年代或画师。

interpretation.en: This is evidence of the book’s illustrated material life, not a portrait of Ibn Sina. The scene connects an influential medical text to the recognizable practice of examining a patient.
interpretation.zh: 这是这部医书图像与物质传播的证据，并非伊本·西那的肖像。画面把一部影响深远的医学文本与具体的病人诊察联系起来。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Wellcome Collection.
note.zh: 公有领域图像。署名：惠康收藏馆（Wellcome Collection）。

title.zh: 绘画肖像中的夸美纽斯

alt.en: A bearded man wearing a dark cap and a coat with a red collar looks outward from a dark painted background.
alt.zh: 有须男子戴深色帽子、穿红领外衣，从深色绘画背景中望向观众。

caption.en: Jürgen Ovens painted Jan Amos Comenius between 1650 and 1670. The portrait belongs to the educator’s later lifetime.
caption.zh: 尤尔根·奥文斯于1650至1670年间绘制扬·阿摩司·夸美纽斯肖像，属于这位教育家生前晚期的形象。

interpretation.en: The close view draws attention to a particular person behind widely circulated educational books. His teaching programme developed through exile, religious commitments and patronage.
interpretation.zh: 近距离肖像让广为流传的教育著作背后的人物成为焦点。他的教育方案在流亡、宗教信念与资助关系中形成。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Rijksmuseum, SK-A-2161.
note.zh: 公有领域图像。署名：荷兰国立博物馆，SK-A-2161。

title.en: Words, numbers and pictures in Orbis Pictus
title.zh: 《世界图解》中的词语、数字与图像

alt.en: An illustrated page headed The World and Mundus places a numbered landscape above parallel English and Latin vocabulary.
alt.zh: 题为“The World”与“Mundus”的图解页，在编号景观下方并列英语与拉丁语词汇。

caption.en: Page 22 of a New York edition published by T. & J. Swords in 1810. This is a later Latin–English edition of Comenius’s book, with Charles Hoole’s translation and cuts credited to Alexander Anderson.
caption.zh: 1810年纽约T. & J.斯沃兹出版版本第22页。这是夸美纽斯著作的后期拉丁语—英语版，采用查尔斯·胡尔译文，插图署名亚历山大·安德森。

interpretation.en: Match the numbers in the picture to the two columns: clouds, birds, hills and people become linked words and things. The page makes the book’s teaching method visible.
interpretation.zh: 将图中数字与两栏词汇对应：云、鸟、山丘和人，把词语与事物连在一起。这一页让书中的教学方法具体可见。

note.en: Public-domain image. Credit: Wellcome Collection.
note.zh: 公有领域图像。署名：惠康收藏馆（Wellcome Collection）。

title.zh: 刻入紫水晶的凯撒侧像

alt.en: A tiny purple gemstone contains a pale profile head; a ruler below shows its small scale.
alt.zh: 微小的紫色宝石内刻浅色侧面头像，下方标尺显示其尺寸。

caption.en: Roman amethyst intaglio, about 50–40 BCE, identified by the Met as a portrait bust of Julius Caesar.
caption.zh: 罗马紫水晶凹雕，约公元前50至40年，大都会将其识别为尤利乌斯·凯撒的胸像。

interpretation.en: A political face could circulate at the scale of a gemstone, as well as in monumental sculpture. The ruler helps recover the intimate size of this ancient portrait.
interpretation.zh: 政治人物的面孔不仅出现于纪念性雕塑，也能以宝石的尺度流传。标尺帮助我们理解这件古代肖像的微小尺寸。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: Rogers Fund, 1911.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：Rogers Fund, 1911。

creator.zh: 未具名罗马宝石雕刻者

title.en: Alexander and Diogenes in a later etching
title.zh: 后世蚀刻画中的亚历山大与第欧根尼

alt.en: An armed ruler and his companions confront a seated philosopher amid architectural ruins and gathered figures.
alt.zh: 一名武装统治者及随从，与坐着的哲学家相对；周围有建筑遗迹和聚集的人物。

caption.en: An anonymous etching, about 1580–1640, imagines Alexander the Great meeting Diogenes. It was made nearly two millennia after Alexander’s lifetime.
caption.zh: 匿名蚀刻画，约1580至1640年，想象亚历山大大帝与第欧根尼相遇，制作时间距亚历山大的生涯近两千年。

interpretation.en: The encounter became a way to contrast political power with philosophical independence. This image shows Alexander’s long afterlife in European art.
interpretation.zh: 这次相遇成为对照政治权力与哲学独立的一种方式。图像展现亚历山大在欧洲艺术中持久的后世影响。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: Gift of Joseph Verner Reed, 1950.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：Gift of Joseph Verner Reed, 1950。

alt.en: A circular bronze medal carries Gutenberg’s imagined bearded profile and inscriptions around its edge.
alt.zh: 圆形铜章上有想象中的古腾堡有须侧像，边缘环绕题字。

caption.en: Anton Scharff’s commemorative medal is catalogued as 1889 (?). It marks the erection of a Gutenberg statue in New York by Robert Hoe, rather than preserving a fifteenth-century likeness.
caption.zh: 安东·沙尔夫的纪念章在目录中标为1889年（存疑），纪念罗伯特·霍在纽约建立古腾堡雕像，而非保存15世纪的本人面貌。

interpretation.en: The medal links the industrial printing world to a celebrated predecessor. It is useful evidence of commemoration alongside the entry’s account of type, ink and presswork.
interpretation.zh: 铜章把工业印刷世界与备受推崇的前辈连接起来，可与条目中的活字、油墨和印刷工艺相互参照，理解纪念行为。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: Gift of Henry N. Kent, 1940.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：Gift of Henry N. Kent, 1940。

title.zh: 1838年绘制的维多利亚加冕肖像习作

alt.en: A young woman wears a jeweled crown in an unfinished oil study, with brushwork left visible around her shoulders.
alt.zh: 年轻女子戴珠宝王冠，未完成的油画习作在肩膀周围保留明显笔触。

caption.en: Thomas Sully painted this oil study during four Buckingham Palace sittings in May 1838. It predates Victoria’s 1858 proclamation transferring government in India to the Crown.
caption.zh: 托马斯·萨利于1838年5月在白金汉宫四次写生时绘制此油画习作，早于维多利亚1858年宣布印度治理转归王室的公告。

interpretation.en: The portrait identifies the sovereign named in the proclamation. Its youthful court image and the later colonial document belong to different moments in a long reign.
interpretation.zh: 肖像标明公告中所称的君主。年轻时的宫廷形象与后来的殖民文件，属于漫长统治中的不同时刻。

items.credit: Bequest of Francis T. S. Darley, 1914

items.creator: Thomas Sully

title.en: Akbar at prayer near the end of his reign
title.zh: 统治末期前后祈祷中的阿克巴

alt.en: An elderly emperor stands in profile holding prayer beads, with a pale robe and a red-and-blue sash.
alt.zh: 年长皇帝侧身站立，手持念珠，着浅色袍服，系红蓝腰带。

caption.en: Early seventeenth-century ink and opaque watercolour. The Met dates its commission to shortly before or after Akbar’s death in 1605; the artist is unrecorded.
caption.zh: 17世纪初的墨与不透明水彩画。大都会认为委托时间在阿克巴1605年去世前后不久；画师未有记载。

interpretation.en: This is the named patron behind the court and translation-workshop entries. Visible changes around the legs also reveal a painter revising the emperor’s presentation.
interpretation.zh: 这是宫廷与翻译作坊条目中的具体赞助者。腿部周围可见的改动，也让我们看到画师调整皇帝形象的过程。

items.credit: H. O. Havemeyer Collection, Gift of Horace Havemeyer, 1929

items.creator: Unrecorded Mughal painter

title.en: Shah Jahan presents his own image
title.zh: 沙贾汗展示自己的肖像

alt.en: A jeweled emperor stands on a small platform inside an ornate album border, holding a portrait pendant.
alt.zh: 佩戴珠宝的皇帝站在小台座上，手持肖像吊坠，四周有精细画册边饰。

caption.en: Chitarman painted this album leaf in 1627–28, near the start of Shah Jahan’s reign. Its portrait precedes his commission for the Taj Mahal.
caption.zh: 奇塔尔曼于1627至1628年绘制此画册页，接近沙贾汗统治开端，早于他委托建造泰姬陵。

interpretation.en: The pendant repeats the ruler’s image inside his portrait. Alongside the mausoleum, it shows another scale at which Mughal patronage made imperial identity visible.
interpretation.zh: 吊坠在皇帝肖像内部再次呈现他的形象。与陵墓相对照，可以看到莫卧儿赞助如何在另一种尺度上呈现帝王身份。

title.en: Abd al-Qadir in an 1879 commemorative print
title.zh: 1879年纪念版画中的阿卜杜勒·卡迪尔

alt.en: A central portrait of a bearded man in a hooded cloak is surrounded by smaller scenes, foliage and lettering.
alt.zh: 戴兜帽、披斗篷的有须男子居中，周围环绕小场景、枝叶与题字。

caption.en: A wood engraving dated 1879, during Abd al-Qadir’s lifetime. Petit Palais credits Edmond Morin and Léon-Louis Chapon as engravers.
caption.zh: 木版画，1879年，制作于阿卜杜勒·卡迪尔生前。小皇宫博物馆将埃德蒙·莫兰与莱昂-路易·沙蓬列为雕刻者。

interpretation.en: The surrounding vignettes turn a portrait into a composed account of a public life. Read this French print alongside the biography’s Algerian and Damascus settings.
interpretation.zh: 周围的小场景将肖像变成经过编排的公共生涯叙事。可将这幅法国版画与传记中的阿尔及利亚和大马士革背景对读。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: Paris Musées / Petit Palais, PPG3829.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：Paris Musées / Petit Palais, PPG3829。

creator.zh: 埃德蒙·莫兰；莱昂-路易·沙蓬

institution.zh: 巴黎博物馆联盟／小皇宫美术馆

alt.en: Tsuda sits in a dark kimono, looking toward the camera above a printed name.
alt.zh: 津田身着深色和服坐着，望向镜头，下方印有姓名。

caption.en: An undated historical photograph reproduced in the National Diet Library’s portrait exhibition.
caption.zh: 日本国立国会图书馆肖像展所收录的历史照片；展览记录未标拍摄日期。

interpretation.en: The portrait introduces the founder of the women’s school that became Tsuda University. Her educational programme linked overseas study with institution-building in Japan.
interpretation.zh: 肖像介绍了后来发展为津田塾大学的女子学校创办者。她的教育方案把海外求学与日本的机构建设联系起来。

note.en: The exhibition explicitly states that all of its images are public domain and that its digitized images may be reused, including commercially, without application. Credit: National Diet Library, Portraits of Modern Japanese Historical Figures.
note.zh: 该展览明确说明所有图像均属公有领域，数字图像可无需申请再次使用，包括商业用途。署名：日本国立国会图书馆“近代日本人肖像”。

alt.zh: 与谢野身着深色和服，衣领带纹样，直视镜头。

caption.en: A historical photograph selected by the National Diet Library for its Yosano Akiko biography; the exhibition does not give an exposure date.
caption.zh: 日本国立国会图书馆为与谢野晶子传记选用的历史照片；展览未给出拍摄日期。

interpretation.en: The image accompanies a career spanning poetry, protest against war and women’s education. The linked library record also leads to her books and manuscripts.
interpretation.zh: 图像伴随一段涵盖诗歌、反战表达与女子教育的生涯。链接的图书馆记录还可引向她的著作与手稿。

alt.en: Fukuzawa poses in a dark Western suit, waistcoat and tie against a plain studio background.
alt.zh: 福泽身穿深色西装、马甲和领带，在素色照相馆背景前摆姿。

caption.en: An undated photograph in the National Diet Library’s historical portrait exhibition. The photographer is not named in the exhibition record.
caption.zh: 日本国立国会图书馆历史肖像展中的未注明日期照片。展览记录未列摄影者。

interpretation.en: Clothing and a studio pose form a public presentation of the educator. Compare that presentation with his arguments about learning and independence.
interpretation.zh: 服装与照相馆姿态共同构成教育家的公共形象，可与他关于学习和独立的论述对照。

note.en: The exhibition explicitly states that all of its images are public domain and that its digitized images may be reused, including commercially, without application. Credit: National Diet Library, Portraits of Modern Japanese Historical Figures.
note.zh: 该展览明确说明所有图像均属公有领域，数字图像可无需申请再次使用，包括商业用途。署名：日本国立国会图书馆“近代日本人肖像”。

title.en: Émilie du Châtelet in a 1751 engraving
title.zh: 1751年雕版画中的埃米莉·杜·夏特莱

alt.en: An oval portrait shows a smiling woman beside part of an armillary sphere, above a lettered pedestal and coats of arms.
alt.zh: 椭圆肖像中的女子微笑坐在部分浑仪旁，下方基座有题字与纹章。

caption.en: An anonymous engraver made this 1751 portrait after Marianne Loir, two years after du Châtelet’s death. Gilles-Edme Petit published the print.
caption.zh: 匿名雕刻者于1751年依据玛丽安娜·卢瓦尔的作品制作此肖像，距杜·夏特莱逝世两年；出版者为吉尔-埃德姆·珀蒂。

interpretation.en: The scientific instrument sits beside aristocratic titles and heraldry. The print brings learned work and social position into the same public image.
interpretation.zh: 科学仪器与贵族头衔及纹章并置，使学术工作与社会地位进入同一公共形象。

title.zh: 吉尔伯特·斯图尔特笔下的华盛顿

alt.en: White-haired Washington wears a black coat and white neckcloth against a dark green background.
alt.zh: 白发的华盛顿身穿黑色外套与白色领巾，背后是深绿色背景。

caption.en: Gilbert Stuart began this oil portrait in 1795, during Washington’s presidency. Technical study shows that the coat was changed from brown to black.
caption.zh: 吉尔伯特·斯图尔特于1795年、华盛顿担任总统期间开始绘制这幅油画。技术研究显示，画中外套由棕色改为黑色。

interpretation.en: Clothing helped construct the president’s public image. The change from American wool to the appearance of European silk velvet makes the portrait a useful study of political self-presentation.
interpretation.zh: 服装参与塑造总统的公众形象。从美国羊毛料改绘为欧洲丝绒的外观，使肖像成为观察政治形象塑造的线索。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1907.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1907。

title.zh: 简·亚当斯与阿尔娃·贝尔蒙特，1912年

alt.en: A pencil drawing shows two seated women in profile, one wearing an elaborate hat.
alt.zh: 铅笔画以侧面描绘两位坐着的女性，其中一位戴着装饰繁复的帽子。

caption.en: Wallace Morgan drew Jane Addams and Alva Belmont in pencil in 1912. The museum identifies both women as social reformers and Belmont as a suffragist.
caption.zh: 华莱士·摩根于1912年以铅笔描绘简·亚当斯与阿尔娃·贝尔蒙特。博物馆将两人列为社会改革者，并将贝尔蒙特列为妇女参政权活动家。

interpretation.en: A shared portrait places Addams beside another reformer rather than isolating her as a solitary public figure. The rapid pencil strokes preserve the character of a drawn encounter.
interpretation.zh: 双人肖像将亚当斯置于另一位改革者身旁，而非将她孤立为单独的公众人物。快速的铅笔笔触保留了现场描绘的特点。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution。

institution.zh: 美国国家肖像馆，史密森学会

alt.en: Sequoyah wears a red turban and blue coat, holds a pipe, and points to characters on a tablet.
alt.zh: 塞阔雅戴红色头巾、穿蓝色外套，衔着烟斗，指向写字板上的字符。

caption.en: This hand-coloured lithograph was published in 1838, during Sequoyah’s lifetime. The museum attributes it to R. T., after Henry Inman and Charles Bird King, with lithography by J. T. Bowen’s firm.
caption.zh: 这幅手工着色石版画于1838年、塞阔雅在世时出版。博物馆将其归于R. T.，仿亨利·英曼与查尔斯·伯德·金的作品，由J. T. 鲍恩公司石印。

interpretation.en: The writing tablet makes literacy the portrait’s central attribute. Its chain of copying and publication shows how an Indigenous inventor’s image circulated through nineteenth-century print culture.
interpretation.zh: 写字板使文字创造成为肖像的核心特征。临摹与出版的链条，展示一位原住民发明家的形象如何在十九世纪印刷文化中流传。

title.zh: 铂金照片中的齐特卡拉-沙，1898年

alt.en: A seated woman with long dark hair and layered necklaces turns her face to the left, one hand raised near her shoulder.
alt.zh: 长发女子佩戴多层项链，坐着转脸望向左方，一只手抬至肩旁。

caption.en: Joseph Turner Keiley photographed Zitkála-Šá in 1898. This glycerine-developed platinum print belongs to the National Portrait Gallery.
caption.zh: 约瑟夫·特纳·凯利于1898年拍摄齐特卡拉-沙。这张甘油显影铂金照片藏于美国国家肖像馆。

interpretation.en: Soft tonal transitions and a deliberately arranged pose show portrait photography as an artistic construction. Read this image alongside her writing and musical work, rather than treating appearance as a summary of her life.
interpretation.zh: 柔和的明暗过渡与精心安排的姿态，呈现肖像摄影的艺术塑造。可将照片与她的写作及音乐工作对读，而不是以外貌概括其生平。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution。

institution.zh: 美国国家肖像馆，史密森学会

title.en: Frida Kahlo through Magda Pach’s eyes
title.zh: 玛格达·帕赫眼中的弗里达·卡洛

alt.en: A painted bust of Kahlo shows pinned-up dark hair, silver earrings and necklace, a red dress and a blue-green background.
alt.zh: 卡洛的半身油画中，她盘起黑发，佩戴银色耳环与项链，穿红色衣服，背景为蓝绿色。

caption.en: Magda Pach painted this oil portrait of Frida Kahlo in 1933. It is a portrait by another artist, not one of Kahlo’s self-portraits.
caption.zh: 玛格达·帕赫于1933年绘制这幅弗里达·卡洛油画肖像。这是另一位艺术家的作品，而非卡洛的自画像。

interpretation.en: Visible brushwork, bright clothing and prominent jewellery shape another artist’s view of Kahlo. Comparing it with her self-portraits opens a question about who controls an artist’s public image.
interpretation.zh: 可见的笔触、鲜艳衣饰与醒目首饰，塑造了另一位画家眼中的卡洛。将它与卡洛的自画像比较，可以追问艺术家的公众形象由谁塑造。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution。

institution.zh: 美国国家肖像馆，史密森学会

title.en: Susie King Taylor introduces her memoir
title.zh: 苏茜·金·泰勒回忆录的卷首肖像

alt.en: Taylor stands in a dark dress, fitted jacket and veil above a printed version of her signature.
alt.zh: 泰勒身穿深色长裙、合身外套并戴面纱站立，下方印有她的签名。

caption.en: The engraved frontispiece of Reminiscences of my Life in Camp, published in 1902, presents Susie King Taylor with her signature beneath the portrait. The maker is unidentified.
caption.zh: 1902年出版的《营地生活回忆录》的雕版卷首肖像，呈现苏茜·金·泰勒，下方印有她的签名。制作者不详。

interpretation.en: A portrait and signature introduce a woman speaking in her own name about slavery, wartime nursing and education. The book is a material link between personal testimony and a public readership.
interpretation.zh: 肖像与签名介绍了一位以自己的名义讲述奴隶制、战时护理与教育经历的女性。这本书将个人证词与公众读者联系起来。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution。

institution.zh: 美国国家肖像馆，史密森学会

title.en: Sarah Winnemucca in a Baltimore studio, 1883
title.zh: 巴尔的摩照相馆中的莎拉·温尼穆卡，1883年

alt.en: Winnemucca stands facing the camera in a fringed outfit and headdress; the photographic mount bears Busey’s Baltimore studio imprint.
alt.zh: 温尼穆卡穿流苏服装、戴头饰，正对相机站立；照片托纸印有布西在巴尔的摩的照相馆名称。

caption.en: Norval Hamilton Busey made this portrait of Sarah Winnemucca in 1883. The albumen silver print retains the studio’s printed mount.
caption.zh: 诺瓦尔·汉密尔顿·布西于1883年拍摄这幅莎拉·温尼穆卡肖像。这张蛋白银盐照片保留了照相馆印制的托纸。

interpretation.en: The studio imprint gives this public image a specific place of production. Its carefully arranged pose can be read alongside Winnemucca’s published testimony and work as an interpreter and educator.
interpretation.zh: 照相馆印记为这一公众形象标明了具体制作地点。精心安排的姿态，可以与温尼穆卡出版的证词及其翻译、教育工作对读。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution。

institution.zh: 美国国家肖像馆，史密森学会

title.en: Carver and a student studying plants

alt.en: Two men wearing hats stand among trees and examine a handful of flowering plants.
alt.zh: 两名戴帽的男子站在树林中，观察手中的开花植物。

caption.en: Clifton Johnson photographed George Washington Carver with a student in Alabama around 1900. The museum identifies the image as a gelatin silver print.
caption.zh: 约1900年，克利夫顿·约翰逊在阿拉巴马州拍摄乔治·华盛顿·卡弗与一名学生。博物馆将图像列为明胶银盐照片。

interpretation.en: The plants between the two figures turn a portrait into a scene of shared inquiry. Carver’s scientific work appears here as observation and teaching, not simply as an isolated achievement.
interpretation.zh: 两人之间的植物，使肖像成为共同探究的场景。卡弗的科学工作在这里表现为观察与教学，而非孤立的个人成就。

note.en: CC0 public-domain image. Credit: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution.
note.zh: CC0公有领域图像。署名：National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution。

institution.zh: 美国国家肖像馆，史密森学会

title.zh: 凯特·谢泼德的1893年选举权报告

alt.en: A cream paper cover carries a decorative border and the printed title Franchise Report for 1893.
alt.zh: 米色封面饰以花纹边框，印有《1893年选举权报告》标题。

caption.en: Te Papa identifies Kate Sheppard as author of this 1893 report, published by the New Zealand Women’s Christian Temperance Union and printed by Ward, Wilson, and Co.
caption.zh: 蒂帕帕博物馆将凯特·谢泼德列为这份1893年报告的作者；出版者为新西兰妇女基督教禁酒联合会，印刷者为沃德、威尔逊公司。

interpretation.en: The cover places the suffrage campaign inside an organized association. Printed reports helped turn local campaigning into a shared national record.
interpretation.zh: 封面将选举权运动置于有组织的社团之中。印刷报告有助于把地方行动汇成共同的全国记录。

title.en: Sālote and Te Puea at Ngāruawāhia
title.zh: 萨洛特与特普埃亚在恩加鲁阿瓦希亚

alt.en: Four women sit in front of six standing men. Sālote sits second from left and Te Puea third from left.
alt.zh: 四名女子坐在六名站立的男子前方。萨洛特坐在左起第二位，特普埃亚坐在左起第三位。

caption.en: The Auckland Weekly News published this group portrait on 7 October 1936. Auckland Libraries identifies Queen Sālote and Te Puea Hērangi in the front row during the Tongan visitors’ stay at Ngāruawāhia.
caption.zh: 《奥克兰周刊新闻》于1936年10月7日刊登这张合影。奥克兰图书馆指出，萨洛特女王与特普埃亚·赫兰吉坐在前排，拍摄于汤加访客在恩加鲁阿瓦希亚停留期间。

interpretation.en: The shared portrait records relationships between Tongan and Māori leaders. Te Puea’s place beside Sālote makes community-building and hosting visible as forms of political work.
interpretation.zh: 合影记录汤加与毛利领袖之间的联系。特普埃亚坐在萨洛特身边，使社区建设与接待来宾作为政治工作的意义清晰可见。

note.en: No known copyright restrictions. Credit: Auckland Libraries Heritage Collections AWNS-19361007-54-02.
note.zh: 无已知版权限制。署名：Auckland Libraries Heritage Collections AWNS-19361007-54-02。

title.en: A map annotated with Ngata’s tribal boundaries
title.zh: 附有恩加塔部族边界标注的地图

alt.en: A North Island map is densely labelled with settlements, waterways and boundaries, with smaller island maps at the upper right.
alt.zh: 北岛地图密布聚落、水道与边界标注，右上角附有较小的岛屿地图。

caption.en: Auckland Libraries dates this photographic copy to 1939 and identifies Āpirana Ngata’s additions showing Māori tribal boundaries at the beginning of the nineteenth century.
caption.zh: 奥克兰图书馆将这份摄影复制图定为1939年，指出阿皮拉纳·恩加塔增添的标注展示十九世纪初的毛利部族边界。

interpretation.en: Ngata’s annotations put historical land relationships onto a government survey map. Read the layers separately: the map’s production date is not the date of the boundaries it reconstructs.
interpretation.zh: 恩加塔的标注将历史土地关系叠加在政府测绘图上。应分别阅读这些层次：地图制作日期并不是它所重建的边界年代。

title.en: Desmond Tutu at the White House, 1984
title.zh: 德斯蒙德·图图在白宫，1984年

alt.en: Desmond Tutu, wearing a clerical collar and dark suit, shakes hands with Ronald Reagan in the Oval Office.
alt.zh: 德斯蒙德·图图身着深色西装、佩戴牧师领，在椭圆形办公室与罗纳德·里根握手。

caption.en: The Reagan Library identifies this White House photograph as Tutu’s meeting with Reagan in the Oval Office on 7 December 1984.
caption.zh: 里根图书馆指出，这张白宫照片记录图图于1984年12月7日在椭圆形办公室与里根会面。

interpretation.en: A formal handshake records access to an international political stage. It documents an encounter, without demonstrating agreement between the two men.
interpretation.zh: 正式握手记录了登上国际政治舞台的机会。它见证一次会面，但并不能证明两人观点一致。

title.en: Kim Dae-jung at an Auckland meeting
title.zh: 金大中出席奥克兰会谈

alt.en: Kim Dae-jung, at right in a dark suit, smiles while shaking hands with Bill Clinton.
alt.zh: 右侧身着深色西装的金大中微笑着与比尔·克林顿握手。

caption.en: Sharon Farmer photographed Kim Dae-jung with Clinton in Auckland on 12 September 1999, before a trilateral meeting with Japan’s prime minister Keizō Obuchi.
caption.zh: 莎伦·法默于1999年9月12日在奥克兰拍摄金大中与克林顿；两人即将与日本首相小渊惠三举行三方会谈。

interpretation.en: The photograph places Kim in regional diplomacy during his presidency. A handshake records the meeting’s public presentation rather than its negotiations or results.
interpretation.zh: 照片呈现金大中任总统期间参与地区外交的场景。握手记录的是会谈的公开呈现，而非谈判过程或结果。

items.institution: Archived Clinton White House website / NARA

note.zh: 莎伦·法默拍摄的白宫公有领域照片。署名：威廉·J.克林顿总统图书馆。

context.en: The classical profile and Latin lettering give scientific authorship a commemorative form. Compare this later image with Newton’s mathematical writing and institutional career.
context.zh: 古典侧面构图与拉丁题字，为科学作者赋予纪念形式。可将这幅后世图像与牛顿的数学著作及机构生涯对读。

context.en: The print shows how a recognisable author’s face accompanied the later circulation of scientific reputation. It belongs to Copernicus’s reception rather than the making of his planetary model.
context.zh: 这幅版画展示了鲜明的作者面孔如何伴随科学声誉传播。它属于哥白尼的后世接受史，而非其行星模型形成时的图像。

context.en: A composed personal portrait offers a different starting point from the familiar lamp-bearing emblem. Her public work also depended on records, training and hospital organization.
context.zh: 这幅沉静的人物肖像，为理解南丁格尔提供了不同于“提灯者”象征的起点。她的公共工作也依赖记录、培训与医院组织。

context.en: Read the book and identifying text as choices made by a later printmaker. Hildegard’s surviving letters provide a separate route into her own community and voice.
context.zh: 书本与身份题字体现后世版画家的选择；希尔德加德存世的书信，则提供通往她本人社群与声音的另一条路径。

context.en: The image gives a face to the engineer named in the separate-condenser story. The contemplative pose is a portrait convention, not a record of the 1769 invention.
context.zh: 图像为独立冷凝器故事中的工程师提供面孔。沉思姿态是一种肖像惯例，并非1769年发明现场的记录。

context.en: This is evidence of the book’s illustrated material life, not a portrait of Ibn Sina. The scene connects an influential medical text to the recognizable practice of examining a patient.
context.zh: 这是这部医书图像与物质传播的证据，并非伊本·西那的肖像。画面把一部影响深远的医学文本与具体的病人诊察联系起来。

context.en: The close view draws attention to a particular person behind widely circulated educational books. His teaching programme developed through exile, religious commitments and patronage.
context.zh: 近距离肖像让广为流传的教育著作背后的人物成为焦点。他的教育方案在流亡、宗教信念与资助关系中形成。

context.en: Match the numbers in the picture to the two columns: clouds, birds, hills and people become linked words and things. The page makes the book’s teaching method visible.
context.zh: 将图中数字与两栏词汇对应：云、鸟、山丘和人，把词语与事物连在一起。这一页让书中的教学方法具体可见。

context.en: Match the numbers in the picture to the two columns: clouds, birds, hills and people become linked words and things. The page makes the book’s teaching method visible.
context.zh: 将图中数字与两栏词汇对应：云、鸟、山丘和人，把词语与事物连在一起。这一页让书中的教学方法具体可见。

context.en: A political face could circulate at the scale of a gemstone, as well as in monumental sculpture. The ruler helps recover the intimate size of this ancient portrait.
context.zh: 政治人物的面孔不仅出现于纪念性雕塑，也能以宝石的尺度流传。标尺帮助我们理解这件古代肖像的微小尺寸。

context.en: The encounter became a way to contrast political power with philosophical independence. This image shows Alexander’s long afterlife in European art.
context.zh: 这次相遇成为对照政治权力与哲学独立的一种方式。图像展现亚历山大在欧洲艺术中持久的后世影响。

context.en: The medal links the industrial printing world to a celebrated predecessor. It is useful evidence of commemoration alongside the entry’s account of type, ink and presswork.
context.zh: 铜章把工业印刷世界与备受推崇的前辈连接起来，可与条目中的活字、油墨和印刷工艺相互参照，理解纪念行为。

context.en: The portrait identifies the sovereign named in the proclamation. Its youthful court image and the later colonial document belong to different moments in a long reign.
context.zh: 肖像标明公告中所称的君主。年轻时的宫廷形象与后来的殖民文件，属于漫长统治中的不同时刻。

context.en: Akbar established the court translation bureau in 1574. This portrait identifies that patron; it does not depict translators at work.
context.zh: 阿克巴于1574年设立宫廷翻译机构。这幅肖像标明该赞助者，并未描绘译者工作现场。

context.en: Akbar developed Fatehpur Sikri as an imperial centre. The portrait adds its named patron to the architectural story.
context.zh: 阿克巴将法泰赫普尔西克里发展为帝国中心。肖像为建筑故事补充了具体赞助者。

context.en: The pendant repeats the ruler’s image inside his portrait. Alongside the mausoleum, it shows another scale at which Mughal patronage made imperial identity visible.
context.zh: 吊坠在皇帝肖像内部再次呈现他的形象。与陵墓相对照，可以看到莫卧儿赞助如何在另一种尺度上呈现帝王身份。

context.en: The surrounding vignettes turn a portrait into a composed account of a public life. Read this French print alongside the biography’s Algerian and Damascus settings.
context.zh: 周围的小场景将肖像变成经过编排的公共生涯叙事。可将这幅法国版画与传记中的阿尔及利亚和大马士革背景对读。

context.en: The portrait introduces the founder of the women’s school that became Tsuda University. Her educational programme linked overseas study with institution-building in Japan.
context.zh: 肖像介绍了后来发展为津田塾大学的女子学校创办者。她的教育方案把海外求学与日本的机构建设联系起来。

context.en: The image accompanies a career spanning poetry, protest against war and women’s education. The linked library record also leads to her books and manuscripts.
context.zh: 图像伴随一段涵盖诗歌、反战表达与女子教育的生涯。链接的图书馆记录还可引向她的著作与手稿。

context.en: Clothing and a studio pose form a public presentation of the educator. Compare that presentation with his arguments about learning and independence.
context.zh: 服装与照相馆姿态共同构成教育家的公共形象，可与他关于学习和独立的论述对照。

context.en: The scientific instrument sits beside aristocratic titles and heraldry. The print brings learned work and social position into the same public image.
context.zh: 科学仪器与贵族头衔及纹章并置，使学术工作与社会地位进入同一公共形象。

context.en: The museum identifies the sitter as George Washington; the 1795 portrait belongs to the presidential phase of this biography.
context.zh: 博物馆确认画中人为乔治·华盛顿；1795年的肖像对应本传记中的总统任期。

context.en: The collection names Jane Addams as a sitter, directly linking this lifetime drawing to her biography.
context.zh: 馆藏记录明确列简·亚当斯为被描绘者，使这幅生前素描与其传记直接相连。

context.en: The museum identifies Sequoyah as the sitter and the tablet as a writing implement, directly connecting the print to this biography of the Cherokee syllabary’s inventor.
context.zh: 博物馆确认被描绘者为塞阔雅，并将写字板列为书写工具，直接对应本条关于切罗基音节文字发明者的传记。

context.en: The museum names Zitkála-Šá as the sitter and identifies her as a writer, violinist and reformer, matching the biography’s subject.
context.zh: 博物馆明确列齐特卡拉-沙为被摄者，并将其列为作家、小提琴家与改革者，与传记主体相符。

context.en: The collection identifies Frida Kahlo as the sitter and Magda Pach as the painter, providing a lifetime portrait directly tied to this biography.
context.zh: 馆藏明确列弗里达·卡洛为被描绘者、玛格达·帕赫为画家，提供与本传记直接相关的生前肖像。

context.en: The museum identifies the frontispiece sitter as Susie King Taylor; her 1902 memoir directly connects the portrait to the literacy, care and freedom discussed in this biography.
context.zh: 博物馆确认卷首肖像的被描绘者为苏茜·金·泰勒；她1902年的回忆录，使图像直接联系本传记讨论的读写、照护与自由。

context.en: The museum identifies the sitter as Sarah Winnemucca and records the Baltimore portrait’s 1883 date, directly linking it to the biography.
context.zh: 博物馆确认被摄者为莎拉·温尼穆卡，并将巴尔的摩肖像定年为1883年，与传记直接相连。

context.en: The museum names George Washington Carver and a student in the photograph, directly illustrating the biography’s account of scientific inquiry and education.
context.zh: 博物馆将照片题名为乔治·华盛顿·卡弗与学生，直接呈现传记中的科学探究与教育工作。

context.en: An authenticated work by Sheppard makes the organizational and publishing side of the suffrage campaign visible.
context.zh: 谢泼德的确证作品呈现选举权运动的组织与出版工作。

context.en: Sālote is explicitly identified, seated second from left. The visit illustrates her relationships across the Pacific.
context.zh: 馆藏明确指出左起第二位坐者为萨洛特。这次访问呈现她的跨太平洋联系。

context.en: Te Puea is explicitly identified, seated third from left, alongside Sālote at Ngāruawāhia.
context.zh: 馆藏明确指出左起第三位坐者为特普埃亚，她在恩加鲁阿瓦希亚与萨洛特并坐。

context.en: The catalogue explicitly attributes additions to Ngata, connecting this map with his work on Māori land and historical knowledge.
context.zh: 馆藏明确将增补内容归于恩加塔，使地图与他对毛利土地和历史知识的工作相联系。

context.en: The gallery explicitly identifies Bishop Desmond Tutu, connecting his biography to international political engagement in 1984.
context.zh: 画廊明确识别德斯蒙德·图图主教，将其生平与1984年的国际政治交往联系起来。

context.en: The White House caption identifies Kim Dae-jung before a trilateral meeting, a specific episode of his presidential diplomacy.
context.zh: 白宫图注明确识别三方会谈前的金大中，记录其总统外交中的一个具体时刻。
